subject: Next steps: log redaction, header handling, and residency requirements
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acme-analytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-05T13:12:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up: logging controls & residency requirements

Vanessa / Monica,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to connect. Quick recap of our priorities from the Acme side so we have a shared checklist: 

- We need request + response logs for debugging, but any PII must be removed before persistence. Specifically: no raw email addresses, no user_id fields that map to identifiable customers, and Authorization-like headers must not be retained.
- Retention: 90-day retention on logs, with automatic purge after that.
- Residency: all logs must reside in US-only storage for this workload (no EU/APAC replication).
- Trace IDs: we need the ability to correlate requests for support, but those IDs cannot be stored in a way that ties back to identifiable users.

Questions for Redwood that would unblock procurement:
1) Do you support header allowlists/deny-lists at the request-logger level? Can we drop/strip headers prior to persistence?
2) What options do you offer for trace-id pseudonymization (one-way hash vs reversible tokenization)? We want to understand the tradeoffs for debugging vs compliance.
3) Can you produce a short sample "scrubbed" log (redacted) showing how you would transform a typical request/response pair?
4) Please attach SOC2 or any relevant compliance artifacts and a short note on how retention lifecycle is enforced.

Next steps: if we can get the sample scrubbed log + answers to the above by EOW Wednesday we can move forward with legal/procurement. Also open to a 30-min technical follow-up with your engineering lead.

Thanks,
Julia Park
Director, Product 
Acme Analytics

--

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Hi Julia — great call, thanks for the clear list. High-level answers and proposed plan below, then Marcus will follow with technical specifics and a sample scrubbed log.

Recap / Answers (short):
- Header handling: yes — Redwood runtime supports configurable allowlist and denylist for headers at the ingress logger. You can choose to strip, hash, or persist only an allowlisted subset.
- Trace IDs: we offer three patterns:
  1) drop entirely at persistence (no correlation)
  2) one-way hashed trace ID using a per-customer salt (non-reversible, allows correlation across requests but not mapping back to user records)
  3) reversible tokenization stored in a customer-managed KMS for support-only use (requires an enterprise key agreement).
- Sample scrubbed log: Marcus will produce a 1–2 request example showing header redaction, body tokenization, and the retained pseudonymized trace id.
- Retention & residency: retention TTLs are enforced at the bucket/DB lifecycle layer (we can configure to 90 days) and we support region-locking to US-only storage for your account/tenant.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) Marcus to share sample scrubbed logs + technical note (today, EOD) — action: marcus_lin
2) Compliance pack (SOC2 + retention policy) to be uploaded to the Drive link and shared — action: vanessa_ortiz (tomorrow)
3) 30-min technical deep dive to validate edge cases (suggest Wed 12/9 11:00am ET) — pls confirm

I'll attach a short proposal PDF that outlines the redaction options and the default behaviors to make review with your security team easier.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Technical note: how we handle request/response logs and pseudonymization

Julia — following Vanessa's note, a focused technical summary and the approach we'll use for the sample scrubbed log.

How Redwood captures logs (configurable):
- Ingestion layer captures request metadata (method, path, headers), body (configurable sampling), response metadata, latency, and an internal trace_id.
- Before persistence we run a configurable pipeline: header filters -> body scrubbing -> tokenization/pseudonymization -> write.

Redaction & pseudonymization options we recommend for your constraints:
- Header handling: implement a denylist for high-risk headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email) and an allowlist for low-risk headers (User-Agent, Accept). Denylisted headers are dropped entirely.
- Trace IDs: use a one-way per-customer HMAC-SHA256 of the trace_id with a customer-specific salt stored in our secrets store. That allows cross-request correlation without reversible mapping back to user profiles. Salt rotation is supported; rotation creates new hashes for new traces while preserving historical correlation only if you opt in.
- Body PII: apply deterministic regex-based tokenization for common PII types (emails, SSNs, phone numbers) and a configurable redaction map for custom fields (e.g., user_id, ssn). We can also offer a pseudonymization layer that replaces tokens with stable aliases if needed.
- Retention/residency: logs are written to a US-only object store with lifecycle rules enforcing a 90-day delete policy. For extra assurance we can turn on immutability windows and audit logs for deletion events.

Edge case we need from you: a few example request headers or a sample raw trace id format that you currently see (if it's not the default UUID) so we can confirm hashing and collision handling. Please redact any real PII when sharing.

I'll upload the sample scrubbed log to the Drive link Vanessa mentioned; it will show the exact transformations. If you prefer a live demo of the scrubber pipeline we can include that in the deep-dive.

--
Marcus Lin
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks, Vanessa and Marcus — that all sounds promising. A couple quick clarifications before we share examples: 

- On the one-way hash for trace IDs: will that still let us correlate multiple requests from the same user/session when we export logs to our internal SIEM? (i.e., does the hash preserve collision-free correlation across systems?)
- If we request reversible tokenization, what are the KMS options and audit controls for key access? We need clear procedures for support access and key rotation.

We're preparing a small canned set of example requests (redacted) to validate the scrubber. We'll upload those to the Drive link by EOD Tuesday.
